message:
feat(directory): the viewer stops adding one to the http port too

The host was converted; the viewer was not, so on an https directory it
still dialled 443 + 1. That is the worse half of the two: the viewer gives
up before it ever calls /api/connect, which is where the relay address
would have come from, so there is no second route either.

The decision now goes through the same rule the host uses, and it lives in
the bootstrap rather than in whoever fills the request -- a caller that
forgets to pass the metadata gets a refusal with a reason, not a dial to a
port nothing answers. A pinned port still wins, http keeps its documented
default, and https with nothing advertised stops and says the server needs
configuring.

The metadata rides on the login response, which the branch reusing a cached
session never sees. Left there, reconnecting would fail on https where a
fresh connect succeeded. That path asks /healthz instead, which carries the
same value and needs no session.

The contract moved into its own header on the way. Including
directory_client.hpp from the viewer's headers dragged winsock in behind
it, and with it the min/max macros, which broke <algorithm> in the next
file along.
